GameDBLocalizedString.Text: At the start of each phase, converts one Limerite into another random resource.
A new batch of neutral units every cycle.
Allows you to build the "Battle Beacon" war machine for your armies.
Adds one more commander for hire. A new commander learns a random ability skill.
Comes with defensive walls, a gate, one slot for defensive upgrades, and two Mindlink Stations. A Mindlink Station grants your units the "Mind Patch" ability, which lets any unit use a ranged attack.
Strengthens the walls and gate. Adds 2 additional Mindlink Stations and 1 more defensive slot.

The toxic wastelands of Old Fossoria are nothing compared to the crystal hellhole the Xenauri once called home. In the Siren System, shelters are built from debris, but they’re just as sturdy as those back home. The memory of meat-grinding storms, carrying clouds of razor-sharp crystal dust, is still painfully vivid.

On the Xenauri homeworld, flora cannot survive outside sheltered greenhouses. So where did that flora come from? From crystal deserts, crystal plains, mountains scattering shards of light for hundreds of miles? Hardly, but that’s the only landscape the Xenauri know. Yet the paintings buried in ancient shelters tell a very different story.

Before the exodus, the Xenauri population was a third of what it had been two hundred years earlier, yet the struggle for resources was fiercer than ever. And still, some denied that the crystal desert was expanding. That’s the danger of a slow-burning catastrophe: by the time you can no longer deny it, it’s already too late.

The last moments were loud, but once the gates of the Mothership closed, a dead silence fell. And in that silence every Xenauri on board realized that, from this moment on, they carried a debt. One life had been redeemed for ten left behind.

It will take some time before the other factions allow the Xenauri to settle. Until then, Limerite is little more than dead weight for a nomadic people. But there are always people willing to forget old grievances when something of real value is put on the table.

The Ssaari of the Xenauri homeworld are deadly, but when there’s nothing else to ride, the laws of the universe dictate that someone will eventually try to ride them. And when the memory of that bloody failure fades, another lunatic will try again, and so on, until eventually you can’t imagine Xenauri without their Ssaari mounts.
Well, if your faction has no gravitors and your Altari insist they have better things to do than waste their powers levitating stuff around the camp, you’ll have to find another way.

Stop wasting your time teaching the Xenauri about recycling. Those people were born on a resourceless world, wearing armor passed down through the generations, and currently living in the repurposed debris of their landing craft. Just ... please stop.

The ever-present scarcity of resources on Xenauri’s homeworld made any form of mass production impossible. Every piece of equipment, weapon, and technological marvel is handcrafted, jealously guarded, and passed down through generations as a precious heirloom.

“Back on the Xenauri world, I had my armor, my saber, and a place to roll out a mattress in my clan’s shelter, and I felt rich! But here in the Siren System, there are beggars who own more than I do. I miss some of the simplicity of the old days.”

The violent nature of the Xenauri planet does not exactly favor traveling on foot. So set aside your prejudice and jump in. The worst-case scenario is a quick death, which is still better than being eaten by a Ssaari lizard whose digestive system was never designed to process organic matter.
In a few years, the Xenauri edge will be dulled by the comforts of life in the Siren System. But for now, they remain as sharp and dangerous as the hostile world that forged them.

Only a small percentage of Xenauri are born with psionic powers, so the number of Altari with true leadership talent is smaller still, not to mention those who possess truly formidable power. Yet the simple fact that their commander is an Altari always boosts the morale of their troops.

In many ways, Xenauri technology resembles that of the ancient Primals. But forget economical, purpose-grown, self-repairing crystal tech; expect years of scouring the wilderness for the right crystals. Still, their generations of experience could prove invaluable to crystal technology research.

Xenauri technology proved surprisingly effective at pushing information through the communication nightmare of the Siren System. Maybe the crystals of their homeworld are somehow related to the crystal-based technology of the ancient Prim... Nah, that would be quite a wild speculation.
Altari librarians guard hundreds of fragile crystals containing knowledge that only they can read. Give them a little drama: drop a glass bottle on the tiles, then run.

Since the dawn of time, Xenauri biotechnology development has been limited by... well, let’s just say the lack of a biosphere on their homeworld. But look at how fascinated they are by the most common clump of grass... They’ll catch up soon enough.

The old mapmakers have mastered special symbols for hundreds of varieties of crystal terrain, yet now struggle to draw little trees. Whoever said a change is as good as a rest deserves a proper kick to the knee.

Altari always considered their powers a natural phenomenon. Only now, after arriving in the Siren System, have they begun to notice fluctuations and anomalies linked to the proximity of the Primals’ ruins. Let’s just say their perspective is slowly beginning to change.

Almost no Xenauri technology can even be operated without psionic powers. But why? Well, when you have someone who can conjure a flame with a simple request, would you really bother inventing a lighter?

Why don’t the Xenauri use ranged weapons? Well, early ranged weapons simply couldn’t penetrate either the scales of their homeworld’s fauna or the heavy armor Xenauri wear for protection against that very same scaly fauna. But don’t worry, they’ll learn as soon as they get their hands on something powerful.

Xenauri armor wasn’t built to protect only against enemy blades, or the teeth and claws of Ssaari. It also shields its wearer from the brutal environment of their homeworld. I don’t know about you, but I’d definitely rather face a crystal shard storm in Xenauri armor than in anything else.

Mines are the embodiment of wasteful warfare. On the Xenauri homeworld, burying an explosive device and waiting for an opponent to step on it, something that may never happen, would be considered absolute lunacy. But as they say, different world, different war.
Xenauri are masterful swordsmen, but when firing guns, they’re more of a danger to themselves than to the enemy. Now that you know this, outsourcing ranged combat is clearly the smartest choice.

It’s surprising how quickly ordinary Xenauri adopted this Hesperidian-made UNSS military technology. Maybe that foolproof, one-button interface really is the best design when you don’t want to get blown up by your own weapon.
There are many kinds of crystals, most with some practical use, and some can even be dangerous. Who would have thought that the latter could be found here in the Siren System?

Are you hungry for some Chickmunk nuggets? Then you’ll have to slaughter one first. But unless you’re an armor-clad Xenauri, I’d recommend tofu instead. You know, tofu won’t try to pluck your eyes out with a diamond-sharp beak... Or did you think I got this eyepatch in some glorious duel?
This is not your ordinary chick. This chick was bred for war! A brutal, fierce pack animal that wants to peck, scratch, and puke its razor-sharp crystal digestion all over its enemies!
When your world is ruled by enormous Ssaari lizards, whose scales can shrug off all handheld ranged weapons, constant movement is the only way to give yourself a fighting chance.

Without the unforgiving selection pressure of their homeworld, they’ll lose their warrior way of life within a few generations, grow soft, and become prey again. But here and now, they’re sharks among sardines, hornets among honeybees. The finest, sharpest blades in the Siren System.

In many shelters, Ssaari Screamers serve as the equivalent of guard dogs. They are gentle with friends and absolutely furious when facing enemies. Their warning scream can wake the entire clan at once, and because they eat crystals, they’re never the reason for an empty storeroom.
A field medic with a well-equipped backpack can work miracles. Who cares whether the medic carried the pack himself or a lizard did, when your veins were leaking and it hurt like hell?

When a Xenauri starts showing signs of being Altari, the entire clan celebrates. Altari are psykers, usually very efficient at destroying things, and if you look at it from the raiders’ perspective, coming from a resource-starved planet, you’ll understand just how important that “destroy things” part really is.

Most Altari are nothing like Akira. Truth be told, the majority are closer to hedge wizards. But even the least formidable among them can take down a skilled swordsman with relative ease. So, for your own sake, keep your comments and comparisons to yourself.

When there’s a distinctive group of individuals, different in appearance or behavior… To hell with euphemisms! Racism! I’m talking about racism! So why don’t most Xenauri treat the Altari like dirt when they’re so different? Because every Xenauri can become Altari, even later in life! The odds are almost zero, but they’re real, and hope is a cruel thing.

The vast majority of Altari become decent psykers. A few come close to Princess-level power! But not you. You’re an Altari Conjurer, something like the local branch manager. It’s not exactly a Blood Ssaari, but riding an old lizard still beats pushing through a crowd of plebeians.
Some Xenauri tried using Firebirds too, but the greatest military achievement of those pioneers was surviving their own livestock. Sometimes it’s better to leave the job to the professionals.

Fowlers are simple creatures with simple lives: eat, sleep, tend the flock, explode something. They treat their birds like family and become deeply offended when someone calls them “ammunition.” “Bird no ammunition!” Then they throw one at the enemy.

In the early stages of Blood Ssaari training, they cannot be mounted. One wrong move can earn you a bite. But once a bond of trust is forged, you won’t find a more loyal friend. Losing a finger or two along the way is just a small price to pay.
The bond between rider and mount ends only in death. Even when one survives the other, they seldom recover. Surviving riders will often seek their own blade; the lizards will simply stop eating.
Clanless outcasts. They all have the same hungry eyes. The same feral grins. Feed them, give them a place to sleep, and they’ll fight for you like the mad dogs they are.
